Strait of Hormuz Status: October 16, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  229 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
16 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.54 + 0.15 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 The New York Times reports Iranian shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are rising, with cargo floating in the water.

02 CNN reports two Singapore-registered container ships were struck in the strait; Marine Insight reports one Singapore-flagged vessel carrying over 2,500 containers sank.

03 Brent crude stood at $105.54, up 0.15% over 24 hours, as of 00:11 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the focal point of a sustained maritime security crisis, with The New York Times, Fox Business, and ABC News all reporting that Iranian shipping attacks in the strait are intensifying and cargo is floating in the water. CNN reports two Singapore-registered container ships were struck in the strait, and Marine Insight reports that one Singapore-flagged vessel carrying over 2,500 containers sank. The Lufkin Daily News reports containers were seen floating in the water after a vessel sank nearby. The New York Times reports that Iran has attacked tankers, yet oil flow through the strait unexpectedly increased, per that outlet. Iran's navy described one burning vessel as a vessel operating in violation of Iranian restrictions, per Middle East Eye. The UAE-managed GFS Pride, whose sinking was previously reported, remains in the news cycle with no new confirmed facts in this window. Brent crude stood at $105.54, up 0.15% over 24 hours, as of 00:11 UTC; WTI stood at $97.44. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, a figure published on that date as part of the weekly series, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. WANA News Agency, an unverified single source, claims the strait will remain closed until Iran's rights are respected; no independent outlet in this feed carries that claim. As of 00:22 UTC, 188 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
